title: Letters Never Sent
subtitle: Drafts found in the lamp room drawer

content.text: Drafts found in the lamp room drawer

I have come to think of the tower less as a building than as a very patient argument against the dark. The gulls nested in the rock below and complained, as they always did, about everything at once. A letter came twice a month by the supply boat, and twice a month I read it standing at the rail.

Storms here do not announce themselves; they simply arrive, the way grief arrives, mid-sentence. I learned to mend the winding gear myself, because the mainland was three hours away on a good sea. The keeper before the keeper before me carved his initials into the stair rail, and I have never sanded them out.

When the light held through a bad night I felt something close to pride, though pride is a poor word for it. The horizon at dusk turned the colour of a bruise healing, violet giving way to a tired green.
